institution: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi
citation: Department of Clinical Microbiology and Immunology, Sir Ganga Ram Hospital. Clinical Microbiology Newsletter, Vol. 23, No. 1: percentage sensitivity, January to December 2016. New Delhi: Sir Ganga Ram Hospital; published June 2017.
reporting: Percent susceptible by specimen (blood, urine, pus wound swab, body fluids, respiratory isolates), organism (Gram-positive and Gram-negative tables) and location (OPD, ward, ICU), with the number of isolates per row; organism counts per specimen and location in bar charts with printed data labels and an "others" list.
method: MIC testing on Vitek 2, interpreted with CLSI 2016 guidelines; colistin percentage sensitivity in Enterobacteriaceae as per the EUCAST guidelines (page 8 highlights, referred to by the "Colistin*" footnote of the blood GNB table); repeat isolates excluded (printed in parentheses).

verification.note: All 10 susceptibility tables (GPC and GNB, pages 2 to 6) were parsed from the PDF text layer (sgrhgrid2.py: pdfplumber word positions; column headers rebuilt from the rotated header text; OPD, ward and ICU taken from each row's background colour and checked against the row order; organism labels assigned to each triple of rows by vertical position), then every cell and every row n was compared by eye with the pages rendered at scale 4 and cropped into left and right halves: no differences; the cells the validator does not keep were re-read (the six caution cells again at scale 6). The "Colistin*" footnote on page 2 and the colistin statement in the page 8 highlights were read from the page. Organism bar charts: bar data labels were matched to the legend by legend order and swatch colour (barcounts.py) and the "others" lists parsed from the text layer inside each panel's box; every panel was checked arithmetically (legend counts plus Others equal the printed Isolates, the "others" list sums to Others, the bar values equal the text-layer data labels) and every panel was compared by eye with the chart rendered at scale 3.2; every recorded row n equals its chart count. Read from the image because the bar parse failed: the three body fluid legends (no bars found; OPD E. coli 25, Klebseilla spp. 15, Staphylococci spp. 12, Others 43; ward E. coli 30, Klebseilla spp. 25, Enterococci spp. 20, Acinetobacter spp. 10, Others 48; ICU Klebseilla spp. 15, E. coli 15, Others 49) and the urine OPD bar labelled 11 (see notes). Second reader 2026-09-26: see issues.

notes: Clinical Microbiology Newsletter of Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, Volume 23, No. 1 (published June 2017), data January to December 2016, 8 pages; the bar-chart layout used in the 2024 file. Pages 2 to 6 give one specimen each (blood; urine; pus wound swab; body fluids; respiratory isolates): organism bar charts for OPD, ward and ICU (samples, positives, isolates, bars with printed data labels and a colour legend, and an "others" list) and Gram-positive (GPC) and Gram-negative (GNB) percentage sensitivity tables with three rows per organism (OPD, ward, ICU, by the colour key) and the number of isolates; "-" means not done. Specimens recorded as blood, urine, pus (printed "Pus wound swab"), sterile (printed "Body fluids") and respiratory (printed "Respiratory isolates"). Rows printed "Staphylococci spp." are separate from Staph. aureus and are recorded as coagulase-negative staphylococci, as the 2011 edition labels the same row "Staphylococci spp. (CONS)"; enterococci ("Enterococci spp.", urine "Enterococcus spp."), Klebsiella and Acinetobacter are reported at genus level. The pus GPC table adds Streptococcus pyogenes rows. Combined columns: "Cefoxitin / Oxacillin" (blood, urine, body fluid and respiratory GPC tables; the pus GPC table prints "Oxacillin" alone, recorded without a combined-column note) is recorded under oxacillin, "Imipenem / Meropenem" (every GNB table) under meropenem, and "Glycopeptide" (body fluids: "Glycopeptides") under vancomycin; each such cell says so in its note. The "Quinolones" column (no agent named) is not recorded; blood Salmonella also print nalidixic acid and chloramphenicol (recorded). Colistin is printed only in the blood GNB table, headed "Colistin*" with the page 2 footnote "*See Highlights for additional comments"; the page 8 highlights state "Colistin percentage sensitivity in enterobacteriaceae is as per the EUCAST guidelines", so the blood E. coli, Klebsiella and Enterobacter colistin figures follow EUCAST while the table note line gives CLSI 2016 for everything else; the P. aeruginosa and Acinetobacter colistin figures have no stated criteria beyond that note line. Each colistin cell says so in its note. Tigecycline is printed as percent susceptible for Enterobacterales and Acinetobacter with no criteria beyond the note line. Isolate numbers: every recorded row n equals its organism's chart count; there are no chart and table mismatches on recorded rows. Two rows printed all "-" (not recorded) disagree with the charts: urine ICU Staphylococci spp. (table n=0, ICU "others" list "Staphylococci spp.-1") and body fluid ICU Staphylococci spp. (table n=2, "others" list 3). Six percentages cannot be produced by the row's n (blood OPD Enterococcus n=15, linezolid 98; blood OPD Enterobacter n=7, Imipenem/Meropenem 63; blood OPD Acinetobacter n=16, Imipenem/Meropenem 52; urine OPD Acinetobacter n=8, Imipenem/Meropenem 90; pus ICU Acinetobacter n=18, Imipenem/Meropenem 4; body fluid ICU Klebsiella n=15, Imipenem/Meropenem 5): per-drug tested numbers are not printed; recorded as printed, with a conflict note on each cell. In the urine OPD chart the bar labelled 11 is drawn in a pale colour that matches no legend swatch; it is recorded as "Morganii spp." (Morganella), the only legend entry without a bar of its own, and the panel then balances (legend 1408 plus Others 59 = 1467 isolates). Organism counts: every legend and "others" entry whose organism has a canonical key is recorded, with misspellings and variants mapped to the intended organism ("Klebseilla spp." and "Klebseilla" as Klebsiella spp., "Serratia marscecens", "Morganii spp." and "Morganii" as Morganella, "E. meningoseptica" and "Elizebethkingia meningoseptica" as Elizabethkingia meningoseptica, "S. maltophila", "B. pseudomallei", "Staphylococci spp." as coagulase-negative staphylococci, "Enterococci spp." as Enterococcus spp.); entries without a key, or that would add to the key of a tabulated organism, are listed in excluded. Where a panel lists one organism twice (blood OPD "Salmonella entertidis-1" and "Salmonella typhimurium-1", both non-typhoidal Salmonella; blood ICU "S. maltophila-2" and "S. maltophilia-7"), each entry is recorded as printed (the build adds counts of the same organism). "Salmonella entertidis" and "Salmonella typhimurium" are recorded as non-typhoidal Salmonella. Fungal isolates are counted in the charts; their susceptibility data were to be published separately in the next issue. Page 1 (psoas abscess due to Salmonella enterica serovar Enteritidis case report; activities), page 7 (prescription auditing of antimicrobials and drug resistance index trends) and page 8 (activities, publications, highlights based on blood isolates in IPD, bibliography, faculty) are not susceptibility tables. The PDF has no direct link: sgrh.com serves it only by an HTTP POST from the Microbiology Newsletter selector on https://sgrh.com/en/publications (issue "June-2017"; the server names the file mb-june2017.pdf); the downloaded file opens completely (8 pages).
issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 1,096 cells, all 111 row n values and all 260 organism counts checked against the PDF: the seeded 25% sample of 274 cells from sample_cells.py (drawn from all 10 GPC and GNB tables on pages 2 to 6) was read blind from the page images (tables at scale 3 cut into halves with the row labels and n kept; small tables at scale 2 to 3) before comparing with the extraction, and every cell, every row n, every row's fill colour and every row label was also compared with an independent parse of the text layer written for this check (cell rectangles by fill colour, values centred in each cell, rotated header text per column, labels by vertical position).

Result: 0 transcription errors, nothing corrected (sample 0 of 274; whole file 0 of 1,096 cells, 0 of 111 n, 0 of 260 counts). OPD, ward and ICU correct on every row (row fills as the colour key, always in OPD, ward, ICU order); the organism label of every row triple is correct, including the pus Streptococcus pyogenes rows; every printed value of a recorded column is in the file; the 12 printed rows not recorded are exactly the 12 rows printed all "-", as excluded says. No table reached the 2% threshold.

Column headers: Cefoxitin / Oxacillin (blood, urine, body fluid and respiratory GPC, 12 cells) and Oxacillin alone (pus GPC, 6 cells) under oxacillin, Glycopeptide and Glycopeptides (36 cells) under vancomycin, Imipenem / Meropenem (68 cells) under meropenem and High Dose Gentamicin (9 cells) under gentamicin_hl match the printed headers, each with its note. Colistin is printed only in the blood GNB table ("Colistin*", 15 cells; the urine, pus, body fluid and respiratory GNB tables have no colistin column); the page 2 footnote "*See Highlights for additional comments" and the page 8 highlight "Colistin percentage sensitivity in enterobacteriaceae is as per the EUCAST guidelines" were read on the images, and the notes on the 9 Enterobacterales cells (EUCAST) and the 6 non-fermenter cells (no stated criteria) say so correctly. The note line on pages 2 to 6 reads 2016 CLSI guidelines.

Charts: all 15 panels re-read from the images and the text layer; every entry agrees with counts or excluded and every panel balances. The urine OPD bar labelled 11 is filled pale cyan, which matches no swatch in that legend (the Morganii spp. swatch is bright blue); it is the 10th bar, Morganii spp. is the 10th legend entry in column order and the only one without a bar, the panel balances only with it (1,408 plus Others 59 = 1,467), and the same pale fill is the Morganii spp. swatch in the 2015 pus OPD legend: the assignment to Morganella is confirmed. The urine OPD "others" list separates "Aeromonas spp.-3" from "Pseudomonas putida-3" with a full stop, not a comma; both are handled. The two chart and table disagreements on rows printed all "-" (urine ICU Staphylococci spp. n=0 against "others" 1; body fluid ICU Staphylococci spp. n=2 against "others" 3) are as printed. Every recorded row n equals its chart count.

Cells not kept: the 6 caution cells (blood OPD Enterococcus n=15 linezolid 98; blood OPD Enterobacter n=7 Imipenem/Meropenem 63; blood OPD Acinetobacter n=16, 52; urine OPD Acinetobacter n=8, 90; pus ICU Acinetobacter n=18, 4; body fluid ICU Klebsiella n=15, 5) and the 22 intrinsic cells (Acinetobacter aztreonam, Proteus nitrofurantoin, Klebsiella and Enterobacter ampicillin) are printed that way, not transcription errors. The page 7 and page 8 figures quoted in excluded match the pages.
